title: Nazareth
era_role: Il punto più oscuro e violento dell'intera discografia iniziale. Mostra il lato predatorio della devozione a Sleep, dove il sacrificio rituale assume i connotati di un'aggressione.
in_character_quotes_gap_reason: Sleep Token ha rilasciato pochissime interviste nel 2016-2018 e mai commenti traccia-per-traccia in-character.

editorial_reading.summary: La critica (Louder, Boolin Tunes) evidenzia come 'Nazareth' sovverta il nome della città della natività cristiana in teatro di un sacrificio cruento e disturbante.
editorial_reading.source_title: Louder - The story behind every Sleep Token song

editorial_reading.summary: ‘I’ll see you when the wrath comes knocking on your bedroom door with money,’ Vessel hisses at one point. It gets more vivid. ‘Let’s load the gun, make her eat the tape in the bathroom mirror,’ he sings in a disconcertingly angelic voice. ‘See if she can guess what a hollow point does to a naked body.’ Literal or metaphorical, they’re unquestionably furious.
editorial_reading.source_title: Louder - The story behind every Sleep Token song (Page 1)

editorial_reading.summary: Cited as the world’s oldest walled city, Jericho has been inhabited for more than 11,000 years. The song that takes its name sees Vessel fixated on a previous relationship – possibly the one referenced in Nazareth. ‘Until I wake, I dine on old encounters,’ he intones. He seems to have moved on, though how that will play out isn’t clear. ‘You taste like new flesh – say my name again,’ he commands at one point. The quick bounce back and comparisons to past events suggest that, once again, it won’t last.
editorial_reading.source_title: Louder - The story behind every Sleep Token song (Page 1)

editorial_reading.summary: With the release cycle for Even In Arcadia, their major-label debut under RCA, the visual and titular aesthetics were refined further, incorporating classical Greek iconographic elements and doubling down on Christian allusions which were present in their early material; though Sleep Token are not a Christian band, “The Way That You Were” is distinctly choral and was filmed in a church, and biblical names such as Nazareth and Eden have been a common avenue for intertextuality. The tracklist includes tracks such as “Gethsemane” and final single “Damocles“, whilst the project title comes from Et in arcadia ego, inscribed on the Shepherd’s Monument via which the first single was teased.
editorial_reading.source_title: Boolin Tunes - The Lore of Sleep Token

editorial_reading.summary: Thanks to Scarlett Heselwood for their suggested chronological placement of “Calcutta” and “Nazareth”.

editorial_reading.summary: In May 2017, it was announced that Sleep Token had signed with independent label Basick Records and would release their second EP Two in July.[5] Ahead of the EP's release, the group issued two new singles – "Calcutta" in May and "Nazareth" in June.[6][7] "Calcutta" received an exclusive premiere through Metal Hammer, where writer Luke Morton described the song as "an odd and unique mix of technical metal and expansive indie soundscapes".[8]

In the 2017 Metal Hammer interview, Vessel revealed that the "markings on his mask" were the band's initials in "ancient runes".[8] He is referring to his original mask, which can be seen in the videos for "Calcutta" and "Nazareth."

callbacks.motif: La violenza del controllo e l'immagine dello specchio/bagno ritornano nelle crisi autolesioniste e relazionali di 'Are You Really Okay?' e 'Ascensionism'.

community_theories.theory: Esistono due scuole principali nella community: (1) Nazareth racconta un ordine diretto di Sleep che costringe Vessel a distruggere una relazione umana reale per restare fedele solo alla divinità; (2) 'lei' è una metafora dell'abuso di sostanze o della memoria traumatica ('eat the tape' = cancellare le prove/ricordi registrati).
community_theories.source_title: Lore of Sleep Token - Two EP & r/SleepToken consensus

community_theories.theory: The EP consist of 3 songs Calcutta, Nazareth, and Jericho. Before releasing the EP, the band had already released both Calcutta and Nazareth as singles on May 5th and June 19th, 2017 respectively.
Nazareth is the second track from Sleep Token's second EP, Two. Nazareth released on July 19th, 2017 with it's official music video.
The song's title is named after the capital city Nazareth, which is located in the Northern District of Israel.[1]

This was revealed in a Sleep Talkin podcast featuring Shaun Hodson of Loki Films, the production company behind several official music videos and cinematic pieces for the band. The band's management didn't approve the original video due to it being too shocking, it had included guns and drugs.[2]
